objective: B313, G15 with G5 and G17. Under the two one-birth-at-a-time rules, join recorded sources on one shared donor and count which keeps ticking. Stop at a pair in which one source ends the other with a measured cost deciding which, or equality for the class, or the first missing construction.
status: Computed on one clock, referee pending; partially successful. Two copies of the scarcity study's ring clock joined on one donor: with no shortfall neither one-birth-at-a-time rule loses a tick. One loose distinction short under recompute-after-every-birth, exactly one of the donor's m proposals goes unpaid and each is last in (m-1)! orders, so a copy loses in proportion to the donor payments its tick needs (12 and 12 of 24; 1,440 and 720 of 5,040); asking first in its own history gives no protection; a tick needing the donor's one-parent birth is lost in every order. The seven-, nine- and 21-knot sources fell outside the 400-birth horizon, and merging two donors needed a repaired construction.
title: Sources that share one supply
